name: Common Blue Violet

facts.how: Raw in salads; flowers candied or as syrup

caution: Eat the leaves and FLOWERS of true violets only. Skip the roots and seeds, and never confuse with unrelated yellow-flowered plants sometimes called violets. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: Heart-shaped leaves and five-petaled blue-purple flowers low in the spring lawn. A gentle, cheerful edible.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: Toss leaves and flowers into salads, candy the blooms for cakes, or steep them into a jewel-colored violet syrup.
